claims.claim: Member profiles are drawn from Congress.gov.
A seat can be held by more than one person across a two-year Congress, which is why there are more profiles than seats.

claims.claim: Every profile is keyed by its Bioguide ID.
House members are identified by bioguide ID directly in the House XML, which is what makes House matching exact.

The stored fields on a member record are the bioguide id, name, party, state, role, district, biography plus its source link, floor statements (comments), voting record, and the two portrait fields. Chamber is derived from role, not stored.

claims.claim: The profile page renders the whole stored vote history, not a truncated slice of it.
Crossovers are surfaced only where the yea-nay margin is within 30% of total yeas plus nays.
claims.sourceSpan: Crossover votes are surfaced only when the yea-nay margin is within 30% of total yeas plus nays.

claims.claim: Outside that threshold crossovers are not computed at all, even where members did cross.
A crossover is a member whose vote differs from their party's majority direction.
A party that splits exactly even has no majority direction, so nobody in it is listed as a crossover.
On the 308-117 House vote on H.R. 139, 117 members voted against their party majority, the margin was 44.9% of yeas plus nays, and none were surfaced as crossovers.
claims.sourceSpan: 119-HR-139, House 2026-07-14, "On Passage" Passed 308-117 — margin 44.9% of yeas plus nays, 117 member(s) voted against their party majority, 0 surfaced as crossovers.

resolution: CONVERGED: pass 7 returned PASS with zero errors and zero warnings, after zero-error passes at 4 and 6. Trust-page audit (Phase B), 2026-08-30/31, across two Opus sessions (the first was killed by a session limit; its draft survived in the gitignored drafts/ and hash-matched this ledger). Seven hostile Sonnet passes, every one adjudicated in the main Opus thread. THE SWEEP FINDINGS: the page said the database covers 552 people (it is 551), claimed a current-term-data field that does not exist in the schema, and claimed same-surname senators were resolved by additional disambiguation logic that had never been written. That last one was fixed in the CODE rather than the prose, and doing so uncovered a live data defect: five senators (Blunt Rochester, Cortez Masto, King, Lujan, Van Hollen) matched nothing on any Senate roll call and showed EMPTY voting records on their public profiles. FOUND DURING THIS AUDIT, ALSO LIVE: detectCrossovers treated an exactly-split party as having a Yea majority, which published Sanders in the Crossed the Aisle list 18 times. Both fixed and backfilled offline before this page was published, so the prose describes shipped behaviour. LATER PASSES: the meta description and index card generalised the House-only bioguide-ID match across both chambers, contradicting the body; the prose rounded 44.9% to 45% on a page about precision; the member-field enumeration read as exhaustive while omitting photo, portraitUrl and bioSource; a claim that two records carry a portrait override was half wrong, because nothing reads portraitUrl; the vote-history claim overstated DEFAULT visibility, since rep.js shows eight rows behind a show-more; and two sentences ranked outcomes rather than describing them - one of them lifted straight from a code comment, which is not an exemption.
notes: THE CODEBASE IS THE SOURCE. Where a claim was false, the fix was chosen deliberately between correcting the prose and correcting the code: the disambiguation claim and the crossover tie were fixed in CODE (they were real defects with live consequences); the member count, the term-data field, the portrait fields, the default row count and the evaluative framing were fixed in PROSE. Nothing was softened. One receipt span had been typed with straight quotes against a stored roll-call file containing curly ones, so it did not resolve literally - repaired by slicing the span out of the file rather than retyping it, which is the general lesson for this ledger.
